name: SE of a single-arm mean from its 95% CI
variables: SE = standard error of the arm mean; UL, LL = upper and lower 95% confidence limits; 1.96 = standard normal 97.5% quantile
notes: For small n (below about 60) replace 1.96 with t_{0.975, n-1}; conversions.se_from_ci is z-based, so use conversions.sd_from_ci(use_t=True) when the goal is the SD.

name: SD from SE of a mean
variables: SD = standard deviation; SE = standard error of the mean; n = arm sample size
notes: Applies to a single-group mean; not to the SE of a between-group difference.

name: SD of a single-arm mean directly from its CI
variables: SD = arm standard deviation; n = arm size; UL, LL = 95% confidence limits; c = critical value (normal, or t with n-1 df for small n)
notes: Combines the two previous steps. The engine uses the t quantile by default (use_t=True), matching the Cochrane Handbook advice for n < 60.

name: SE of a between-arm difference from its 95% CI
variables: SE_diff = standard error of the mean difference between arms; UL, LL = 95% confidence limits of that difference
notes: For small trials use t(0.975, n1 + n2 - 2) instead of 1.96 (Cochrane Handbook §6.5.2.3); conversions.se_from_ci is z-based only.

name: Pooled arm SD from the SE of a between-arm difference
variables: SD_pooled = common within-arm SD; SE_diff = SE of the mean difference; n1, n2 = arm sizes
notes: Assumes equal SDs in both arms. No dedicated engine function; the same division is performed inside conversions.sd_diff_from_t (which starts from a t statistic).

name: Hozo mean from median and range
variables: a = minimum; m = median; b = maximum; n = sample size
notes: Call with method='hozo' for (a + 2m + b)/4; the engine applies it for any n, so the n > 25 rule (use the median) must be applied by hand. The engine default is Luo et al. 2018, which performs better. The source cites Hozo also for IQR data, which Hozo does not cover.

name: Hozo variance from median and range (n <= 15)
variables: Var = estimated variance; a = minimum; m = median; b = maximum
notes: Hozo's rule for very small samples (n <= 15). Not implemented; the engine's conversions.sd_from_median uses Wan et al. 2014 instead.

name: Hozo SD from range (15 < n <= 70)
variables: SD = estimated standard deviation; a = minimum; b = maximum; n = sample size
notes: Not implemented as such; conversions.sd_from_median (Wan 2014) is the engine's n-dependent replacement.

name: Hozo SD from range (n > 70)
variables: SD = estimated standard deviation; a = minimum; b = maximum; n = sample size
notes: Not implemented as such; conversions.sd_from_median (Wan 2014) is the engine's n-dependent replacement.

name: SD from interquartile range (Wan 2014; IQR/1.35 under normality)
variables: SD = estimated standard deviation; Q1, Q3 = first and third quartiles; n = sample size; Phi^-1 = standard normal quantile function; eta(n) = expected IQR of n standard normal draws
notes: Not from Hozo 2005 (which covers range only), contrary to the source's citation. conversions.sd_from_median(n, q1=..., q3=...) implements the Wan et al. 2014 eta(n) form; IQR/1.35 is its large-sample limit. Luo 2018 / Shi 2020 are alternatives for the mean.

name: Pooled standard deviation
variables: s_p = pooled SD; sd1, sd2 = arm SDs (here SDs of mean change); n1, n2 = arm sizes; N = n1 + n2

name: Cohen's d
variables: d = standardized mean difference without small-sample correction; m1, m2 = arm means (here mean net changes); s_p = pooled SD
notes: Use effect_sizes.smd(..., correct=False). Stata metan's default SMD is Cohen's d. The source mislabels the measure 'standard mean difference' and never says whether d or g was used.

name: Variance of Cohen's d
variables: Var(d) = sampling variance of d; n1, n2 = arm sizes; N = n1 + n2
notes: Equals the engine's vtype='LS' with correct=False (1/n1 + 1/n2 = N/(n1 n2)). Stata metan uses d^2 / (2(N - 2)) as the second term.

name: Hedges' small-sample correction factor J (approximation)
variables: J = correction factor; N = n1 + n2 (total sample size); N - 2 = degrees of freedom
notes: effect_sizes.hedges_j takes df = N - 2, not N. Its default is the exact gamma-function J (method='exact'); method='approx' gives this formula. Example: N = 30 gives J ~ 0.973.

name: Hedges' g
variables: g = bias-corrected SMD; J = small-sample correction factor; d = Cohen's d
notes: effect_sizes.smd(..., correct=True) is the engine default. Stata metan gives g with the hedges option.

name: Variance of Hedges' g
expression: Var(g) = J^2 * Var(d)   or approximately   N / (n1 * n2) + g^2 / (2N)
variables: Var(g) = sampling variance of g; J = correction factor; Var(d) = variance of d; n1, n2 = arm sizes; N = n1 + n2
notes: vtype='LS2' gives J^2 Var(d) (Borenstein 2009); vtype='LS' gives the approximation (metafor default). Stata metan uses g^2 / (2(N - 3.94)) as the second term.

name: SD of change from baseline and final SDs
expression: SD_change = sqrt( SD_pre^2 + SD_post^2 - 2 * r * SD_pre * SD_post )
variables: SD_change = SD of the within-person change; SD_pre, SD_post = baseline and end SDs; r = pre-post correlation
locator: p. 2 §2.2; p. 2 §2.5 (needed by inclusion criterion 4; formula [EXTERNAL])
notes: r is commonly imputed as 0.5 with a sensitivity analysis over 0.2-0.8. The source reports neither r nor a sensitivity analysis. conversions.corr_from_change back-calculates r from a fully reported trial.

name: SE back-calculated from a pooled 95% CI
variables: SE = standard error of the pooled estimate; UL, LL = printed 95% confidence limits
notes: Valid only for symmetric Wald-type CIs on the analysis scale. With CI limits rounded to 2 decimals the SE can be off by up to about 0.003 (0.01/3.92). 2 * 1.959964 = 3.919928.

name: z statistic and two-sided p from estimate and SE
variables: z = Wald statistic; estimate = pooled SMD; SE = its standard error; Phi = standard normal CDF; p = two-sided p-value
notes: Example: MDA SMD -0.53, SE 0.1709 gives z = -3.10, p = 0.0019.

name: Fixed-effect inverse-variance weights and pooled mean
expression: w_i = 1 / v_i;   y_FE = sum(w_i * y_i) / sum(w_i)
variables: w_i = weight of study i; v_i = within-study variance; y_i = study effect size; y_FE = fixed-effect pooled estimate
notes: First step of the DL procedure; model='fixed' in the engine. The source reports no fixed-effect analysis.

name: Cochran's Q
expression: Q = sum( w_i * (y_i - y_FE)^2 ),  df = k - 1
variables: Q = heterogeneity statistic; w_i = 1/v_i; y_i = study effect; y_FE = fixed-effect estimate; k = number of studies
notes: The source says the Q test was used but prints no Q, df or p.

name: DL scaling constant C
variables: C = scaling constant of the DL estimator; w_i = 1/v_i
notes: Returned as 'C' by models.heterogeneity; also computed inside models.tau2_dl.

name: DerSimonian-Laird between-study variance
variables: tau^2_DL = DL estimate of between-study variance; Q = Cochran's Q; df = k - 1; C = scaling constant
notes: Truncated at zero. [note: use DL only to reproduce the source. The Cochrane Handbook v6 favours REML or Paule-Mandel (models.tau2_reml, models.tau2_pm), and DL tends to underestimate tau^2 when heterogeneity is large.]

name: Random-effects weights, pooled estimate and SE
expression: w*_i = 1 / (v_i + tau^2);   mu = sum(w*_i * y_i) / sum(w*_i);   SE(mu) = 1 / sqrt(sum(w*_i))
variables: w*_i = random-effects weight; v_i = within-study variance; tau^2 = between-study variance; y_i = study effect; mu = pooled random-effects estimate
notes: Reproduce the source with models.meta_analysis(yi, vi, model='random', tau2_method='DL', ci_method='z'); the engine default is REML with HKSJ.

name: Wald confidence interval for the pooled estimate
variables: mu = pooled estimate; SE(mu) = its standard error; 1.96 = standard normal 97.5% quantile
locator: p. 7 Table 2 (inferred from CI symmetry; formula [EXTERNAL])
notes: ci_method='z'. The CI method is not stated in the source; symmetry of the printed CIs is consistent with it (Stata metan default). [note: with few studies the Wald CI is too narrow; an HKSJ-type CI (engine default ci_method='hksj') is advisable for new analyses.]

name: Prediction interval (random effects)
variables: mu = pooled estimate; t_{k-2, 0.975} = t quantile with k - 2 df; tau^2 = between-study variance; SE(mu) = SE of mu; k = number of studies
notes: Not reported by the source. Engine: pi_method='t_k-2' (needs k >= 3). The engine plugs in the SE of the chosen CI method (HKSJ SE by default); pass ci_method='z' to get exactly this formula.

name: I-squared
variables: I^2 = proportion of total variability due to heterogeneity; Q = Cochran's Q; df = k - 1
notes: The source prints I^2 with 1 decimal (TBARS as '00.0%'). The engine also returns Higgins-Thompson and Q-profile CIs for I^2.

name: H-squared
variables: H^2 = ratio of observed to expected dispersion; Q = Cochran's Q; df = k - 1
notes: Not reported by the source; returned as 'H2' by models.heterogeneity.

name: Cochran's Q implied by a printed I^2
variables: Q = implied Cochran's Q; df = k - 1; I^2 = printed I-squared in %
notes: Reviewer cross-check, valid when I^2 > 0; for I^2 = 0 only Q <= df follows. Examples: MDA 18/(1-0.883) = 153.8; TRAP 2/(1-0.813) = 10.7. Assumes the printed k is the number of pooled comparisons.

name: CI midpoint symmetry check
variables: LL, UL = printed confidence limits; estimate = printed pooled SMD
notes: With 2-decimal printing, agreement within 0.005 is expected for a symmetric (Wald, t or HKSJ) interval; larger gaps suggest a back-transformed scale, a non-Wald interval or a typo.

name: Test for subgroup differences (Q_between)
expression: Q_between = sum_g W_g * (mu_g - mu_w)^2,  W_g = 1 / SE(mu_g)^2,  mu_w = sum_g(W_g * mu_g) / sum_g(W_g),  df = G - 1
variables: mu_g = pooled estimate in subgroup g; SE(mu_g) = its standard error (for a Wald SE, W_g = sum of the w*_i in g); mu_w = weighted mean of the subgroup estimates; G = number of subgroups
notes: Not reported by the source. This is the RevMan / Borenstein ch. 19 form that moderators.subgroup_analysis computes; under a common-effect model mu_w equals the overall estimate. The engine uses each subgroup's reported SE, so pass ci_method='z' for Wald SEs, and state whether tau^2 is common (common_tau2=True) or separate per subgroup.

name: Egger's regression test
expression: y_i / SE_i = b0 + b1 * (1 / SE_i) + e_i;   H0: b0 = 0
variables: y_i = study effect; SE_i = its standard error; b0 = intercept (asymmetry); b1 = slope; e_i = residual
notes: OLS fit; two-sided p < 0.10 is the conventional threshold; low power below about 10 studies (the engine warns when k < 10). The source applied it with k = 3-19 and printed no statistics.

name: Modified SE for SMD funnel-asymmetry tests
variables: SE_mod = SE of the SMD without the d-dependent term; n1, n2 = arm sizes; N = n1 + n2
notes: Avoids spurious asymmetry caused by the dependence of the SMD's SE on d. No dedicated engine option; it can be supplied manually as the precision measure.

name: Begg-Mazumdar rank correlation test
expression: t*_i = (y_i - y_FE) / sqrt(v_i - 1/sum(w_i));   tau_K = Kendall tau(t*_i, v_i)
variables: t*_i = standardized effect; y_i = study effect; y_FE = fixed-effect estimate; v_i = within-study variance; w_i = 1/v_i; tau_K = Kendall's rank correlation
locator: p. 7 §3.3 (test named in results only; formula [EXTERNAL])
notes: Less powerful than Egger's test. The source lists Begg's test in the results but not in the methods.
